children: latest takeover proposal, its third rejection of the investment firm. The A$3-per-share offer valued the student placement company and IELTS exam co-owner at approximately A$833.7 million ($564.5 million).

IDP’s board said the bid substantially underestimated the company’s value and was too low to justify further discussions. Blackstone’s revised price was between 20% and 30% above its previous two offers.

For investors, the rejection highlights a gap between IDP’s confidence in a recovery and its current earnings outlook. Shareholders face continued uncertainty as the board holds out for greater value despite deteriorating industry conditions. The company reported an almost 75% decline in annual statutory net profit in August and projected lower operating earnings for fiscal 2027.

IDP expects market volumes to shrink again in fiscal 2027, reflecting the downturn in international education. Nevertheless, management believes student volumes can return to sustainable growth over the next several years.

title: Australia's IDP Education rejects Blackstone’s sweetened takeover bid
